title: Check: Deployments and ReplicaSets
description: Five questions on rollouts, ownership and rollbacks.

questions.prompt: What is the ownership chain when you create a Deployment?
questions.explanation: The Deployment manages ReplicaSets; each ReplicaSet keeps its own Pods alive. A rollout is one ReplicaSet scaling up while another scales down.

questions.prompt: You change the image in a Deployment. What does the Deployment controller do?

options.text: Edits the existing Pods in place
Creates a new ReplicaSet and shifts replicas to it
Deletes every Pod, then recreates them
Nothing until you scale it manually

questions.explanation: Pods are immutable in the fields that matter, so a new template means a new ReplicaSet. The old one scales down as the new one scales up.

questions.prompt: Write the command that undoes the last rollout of a Deployment named web.
questions.explanation: Old ReplicaSets are kept precisely so a rollback is a scale-up of the previous one.

questions.prompt: Write the command that watches the progress of that rollout.
questions.explanation: `rollout status` blocks until the rollout finishes or fails, which makes it useful in scripts as well as by hand.

questions.prompt: Which status field tells you whether the controller has seen your latest change?
questions.explanation: `observedGeneration` lagging behind `metadata.generation` means the controller has not processed your edit yet.
